title: Signature Golden Hour Tea Blend
description: The Signature Golden Hour Tea Blend is an original Signature drink design built around honey as the whole sweetener, with no refined sugar anywhere in the cup. It pairs a mild wildflower honey with chamomile and a thin slice of orange, so the honey flavor leads and the citrus lifts it rather than covering it. The blend is designed as an evening drink: warm, gently sweet, and simple enough to make in five minutes with one pot and one spoon. Its Signature character is the orange-and-chamomile pairing, chosen to show off a light honey instead of hiding it behind strong spice.
ingredients: 1 chamomile tea bag or 1 tablespoon dried chamomile
method: Boil water and pour it over the chamomile and orange slice in a cup.
Steep for four minutes, then lift out the chamomile.
Stir in the honey until it disappears completely.
Taste: add a second teaspoon of honey only if the orange makes the cup too tart.
Serve warm, in the evening, with the orange slice left in the cup.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat.
storage: Store honey sealed at room temperature; store dried chamomile in a dry, airtight tin away from light.
variations: Morning version: swap chamomile for green tea and keep the same honey amount.
Iced version: make a double-strength hot brew, dissolve the honey hot, then pour over ice.
Spiced version: add one thin slice of fresh ginger to the steep.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Golden Hour Tea Blend'
CUPS = [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0]
for sugar in CUPS:
    honey = sugar * 0.75
    liquid_cut_tbsp = sugar * 3
    print("%s cups sugar -> %.2f cups honey, cut liquid by %.0f tbsp" % (sugar, honey, liquid_cut_tbsp))
print("Rule: use 3/4 cup honey per 1 cup sugar, cut other liquid, lower oven by 25 F.")
demo.expected_output:
0.5 cups sugar -> 0.38 cups honey, cut liquid by 2 tbsp
1.0 cups sugar -> 0.75 cups honey, cut liquid by 3 tbsp
1.5 cups sugar -> 1.12 cups honey, cut liquid by 4 tbsp
2.0 cups sugar -> 1.50 cups honey, cut liquid by 6 tbsp
Rule: use 3/4 cup honey per 1 cup sugar, cut other liquid, lower oven by 25 F.

title: Signature Honey-Rye Harvest Cake
description: The Signature Honey-Rye Harvest Cake is an original Signature bake that pairs dark wildflower honey with rye flour, a combination chosen because rye's earthy flavor stands up to strong honey instead of being buried by it. The cake is built as a one-bowl loaf: honey and butter melted together, rye and wheat flour folded in, and a handful of toasted walnuts for texture. It is designed to improve over two days, as the honey moisture settles through the crumb, so it is baked ahead and sliced only when needed. The Signature character is the rye-and-dark-honey pairing and the two-day rest, which turns a simple loaf into a keeping cake.
ingredients: 150 g rye flour and 150 g wheat flour
method: Melt the honey and butter together in a pan over low heat and cool slightly.
Whisk in the eggs, then fold in both flours and the baking soda.
Fold in the walnuts, pour into a lined loaf pan, and bake at 325 degrees Fahrenheit for 55 minutes.
Check with a skewer; it should come out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
Cool in the pan for ten minutes, turn out, wrap, and rest for two days before slicing.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat.
storage: Wrap the loaf airtight and keep at room temperature for up to a week; the flavor deepens over the first two days.
variations: Apple version: fold in one diced apple and reduce the honey by 30 g.
Seed version: top the loaf with pumpkin seeds before baking.
Mini loaves: divide the batter into three small pans and bake for 35 minutes.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Honey-Rye Harvest Cake'
BASE_HONEY_G = 300
SCALE = [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]
for s in SCALE:
    print("Scale %.1fx: honey %d g, flour %d g, soda %.1f tsp" % (s, BASE_HONEY_G * s, 300 * s, 1.0 * s))
print("Honey cakes brown faster: check 10 minutes before the recipe time.")
demo.expected_output:
Scale 0.5x: honey 150 g, flour 150 g, soda 0.5 tsp
Scale 1.0x: honey 300 g, flour 300 g, soda 1.0 tsp
Scale 1.5x: honey 450 g, flour 450 g, soda 1.5 tsp
Honey cakes brown faster: check 10 minutes before the recipe time.

title: Signature Ember Honey Glaze for Roast Roots
description: The Signature Ember Honey Glaze is an original Signature glaze designed for roast root vegetables rather than meat, built on smoked paprika and cider vinegar to give honey a savory, campfire edge. It is deliberately thick, so it clings to carrots, parsnips, and sweet potatoes instead of pooling in the pan, and it is applied twice: once halfway through roasting and once at the end. The Signature character is the smoked-paprika-and-cider pairing, which makes the glaze taste savory first and sweet second, the reverse of most honey glazes. It is a vegetable-first design, and it works equally well on roasted squash and cauliflower.
method: Whisk the honey, vinegar, paprika, oil, and salt until smooth and thick.
Toss cut root vegetables in half the glaze and roast at 400 degrees Fahrenheit for 25 minutes.
Turn the vegetables, brush with the remaining glaze, and roast for 15 minutes more.
Check that the glaze is dark and glossy, not black; pull the pan early if the edges darken too fast.
Serve hot, with any pan glaze spooned over the top.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat.
storage: Store leftover glaze refrigerated for up to a week; re-whisk before using, since honey glazes thicken when cold.
variations: Cauliflower version: use the same glaze on florets and roast for 20 minutes total.
Squash version: add a pinch of cinnamon to the glaze for butternut squash.
Grill version: brush the glaze on vegetables on a grill in the last five minutes only.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Ember Honey Glaze for Roast Roots'
PER_KG_G = 80
WEIGHTS = [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]
for w in WEIGHTS:
    print("%.1f kg -> %d g glaze (%d g honey, %d g mustard)" % (w, PER_KG_G * w, PER_KG_G * w * 0.6, PER_KG_G * w * 0.4))
print("Brush glaze on in the last 15 minutes so the honey does not burn.")
demo.expected_output:
0.5 kg -> 40 g glaze (24 g honey, 16 g mustard)
1.0 kg -> 80 g glaze (48 g honey, 32 g mustard)
1.5 kg -> 120 g glaze (72 g honey, 48 g mustard)
Brush glaze on in the last 15 minutes so the honey does not burn.

title: Signature Moon-Garden Metheglin
description: The Signature Moon-Garden Metheglin is an original Signature mead design flavored with chamomile and lemon balm, herbs chosen because their gentle floral character suits honey instead of fighting it. It is built as a medium-strength mead, with a honey-to-water ratio that ferments dry and then ages with the herbs for a calm, garden-like finish. The design deliberately avoids strong spice, so the honey variety remains the lead flavor and the herbs act as a background note. It is an adult drink, made with the same clean fermentation practice as any mead, and it is meant to be aged at least six months before tasting.
ingredients: A fermenter with an airlock and a hydrometer
method: Dissolve the honey in warm water, cool to room temperature, and pour into a sanitized fermenter.
Add yeast nutrient, pitch the yeast, and fit the airlock.
Ferment at 60 to 70 degrees Fahrenheit for three weeks, then rack off the sediment.
Add the chamomile and lemon balm in a sanitized mesh bag and steep for one week, then remove the bag.
Age for six months, bottle, and label with the date before storing cool.
safety: Alcoholic drink for adults only. Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Sanitize all equipment and never seal a fermenting vessel airtight.
storage: Store bottled metheglin in a cool, dark place for at least six months before opening; it keeps for several years.
variations: Strong version: increase the honey to 4.5 kg for a richer, sweeter finish.
Dry version: ferment to a final gravity below 1.005 and skip the herb steep.
Fruit version: add 1 kg of berries at the herb stage for a melomel-methelgin blend.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Moon-Garden Metheglin'
HONEY_KG = 3.5; WATER_L = 12.0; FG = 1.008
lbs = HONEY_KG * 2.20462; gal = WATER_L * 0.264172
og = 1 + (lbs * 35 / gal) / 1000.0
abv = (og - FG) * 131.25
print("Honey %.1f kg in %.1f L water" % (HONEY_KG, WATER_L))
print("Estimated original gravity: %.3f" % og)
print("Estimated ABV at FG %.3f: %.1f%%" % (FG, abv))
print("Estimate only: measure with a hydrometer; fermentation varies with yeast and temperature.")
demo.expected_output:
Honey 3.5 kg in 12.0 L water
Estimated original gravity: 1.085
Estimated ABV at FG 1.008: 10.1%
Estimate only: measure with a hydrometer; fermentation varies with yeast and temperature.

title: Signature Orchard Braggot and Cider-Honey Vinegar
description: The Signature Orchard Braggot and Cider-Honey Vinegar is an original Signature pair of products built around one orchard idea: apple and honey belong together, in beer and in vinegar alike. The braggot uses pale malt, light honey, and apple juice in place of part of the water, giving a crisp drink with apple aroma behind the honey. The vinegar uses the same pairing in reverse, fermenting honey and apple juice into wine and then into a floral apple-honey vinegar for dressings. The Signature character is the shared apple-and-honey base across two different fermentations, so one orchard harvest yields both a drink and a pantry staple.
ingredients: 5 L apple juice and 5 L water
Vinegar mother for the vinegar batch
method: Brew the malt wort, add the apple juice and honey, and ferment with beer yeast for two weeks.
Condition the braggot for four weeks, then bottle and label.
For the vinegar, ferment honey and apple juice with wine yeast into wine, then add a vinegar mother under cloth cover.
Taste the vinegar weekly for four to eight weeks until sharply acidic, then bottle.
Store both products cool and label each with its date.
safety: Braggot is an alcoholic drink for adults only. Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Discard any batch with mold or a rotten smell; vinegar is a food ingredient, not a medical treatment.
storage: Store the braggot cool and dark for up to a year; store the vinegar sealed at room temperature for a year or more.
variations: Pear version: swap apple juice for pear juice in both products.
Spiced vinegar: steep one cinnamon stick in the finished vinegar for a week.
Strong braggot: raise the honey to 2.5 kg for a richer finish.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Orchard Braggot and Cider-Honey Vinegar'
HONEY_KG = 1.5; MALT_KG = 2.0; WATER_L = 10.0; FG = 1.01
lbs_h = HONEY_KG * 2.20462; lbs_m = MALT_KG * 2.20462; gal = WATER_L * 0.264172
og = 1 + (lbs_h * 35 + lbs_m * 29) / gal / 1000.0
print("Honey %.1f kg + malt %.1f kg in %.1f L" % (HONEY_KG, MALT_KG, WATER_L))
print("Estimated original gravity: %.3f" % og)
print("Estimated ABV at FG %.3f: %.1f%%" % (FG, (og - FG) * 131.25))
demo.expected_output:
Honey 1.5 kg + malt 2.0 kg in 10.0 L
Estimated original gravity: 1.092
Estimated ABV at FG 1.010: 10.8%

title: Signature Honeycomb Crunch Bars
description: The Signature Honeycomb Crunch Bar is an original Signature candy that starts from classic honeycomb candy and finishes it as a dipped, nut-topped bar instead of loose chunks. The honeycomb core is boiled to hard crack with dark honey for a deeper caramel note, then cut into bars, dipped in dark chocolate, and scattered with toasted hazelnuts while the chocolate is still wet. The design goal is contrast: shattering crisp sponge against smooth chocolate and crunchy nuts, with honey flavor in every layer. It is a hot-sugar project, so it is made with a thermometer, a heavy pan, and full attention, and it is portioned as bars so each piece is a single serving.
method: Boil the honey, sugar, and water to 300 degrees Fahrenheit in a heavy pan, stirring only until the sugar dissolves.
Remove from heat, whisk in the baking soda in one quick motion, and pour into a lined pan without stirring or scraping.
Cool fully, then cut the sponge into bars.
Melt the chocolate, dip each bar halfway, and scatter hazelnuts over the wet chocolate.
Set the bars on parchment until the chocolate hardens, then wrap individually.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Hot sugar causes serious burns: keep children away from the stove and use oven mitts.
storage: Store the bars airtight at room temperature for up to three weeks; humidity softens the honeycomb core, so keep them dry.
variations: Milk chocolate version: dip in milk chocolate and top with crushed almonds.
Salt version: sprinkle flaky salt over the wet chocolate instead of nuts.
Mini version: cut the sponge into bite-size cubes before dipping.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Honeycomb Crunch Bars'
STAGES = [('Soft ball', 235, 245), ('Firm ball', 245, 250), ('Hard crack', 300, 310)]
BATCH_G = 600
for name, lo, hi in STAGES:
    print("%s: %d-%d F" % (name, lo, hi))
print("Batch %d g honeycomb candy at soft-crack needs %d g sugar base" % (BATCH_G, int(BATCH_G * 0.6)))
print("Use a candy thermometer; honey browns fast past 300 F.")
demo.expected_output:
Soft ball: 235-245 F
Firm ball: 245-250 F
Hard crack: 300-310 F
Batch 600 g honeycomb candy at soft-crack needs 360 g sugar base
Use a candy thermometer; honey browns fast past 300 F.

title: Signature Rosehip and Lavender Infused Honeys
description: The Signature Rosehip and Lavender Infused Honeys are an original Signature pair of infused honeys designed as a set: one tart and fruity, one floral and calm, both built on the same light honey so the infusions can be compared side by side. The rosehip honey steeps dried rosehips for a tart, berry-like note that suits tea and yogurt, while the lavender honey steeps culinary lavender briefly, so it stays floral without turning soapy. Both are made by the same method, steeped in sealed jars and tasted weekly, and both are labeled as a matched pair. The Signature character is the pairing itself: two infusions, one base honey, designed to be tasted together.
ingredients: 1 kg light wildflower honey, split into two jars
Two sterilized glass jars with tight lids
method: Warm the honey gently until it flows freely, then divide it between two sterilized jars.
Add rosehips to one jar and lavender to the other, seal both, and label with contents and date.
Steep in a cool, dark place for three weeks, turning each jar weekly.
Taste weekly: remove the lavender after two weeks if the floral note is strong, and leave the rosehips for the full three weeks.
Strain through a fine sieve, rebottle, and label again before storing.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Use culinary lavender only, and keep all flavorings dry; discard any jar that bubbles or smells of alcohol.
storage: Store both infused honeys sealed in a cool, dark place for up to a year; crystallization is normal and reversible.
variations: Single-jar version: make only the rosehip honey for tea.
Gift set: bottle both honeys in small jars with tasting notes.
Herb version: swap lavender for dried rosemary for a savory infused honey.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Rosehip and Lavender Infused Honeys'
FRUIT_G = 500; HONEY_G = 500; SEED_PCT = 10
print("Honey-preserved fruit: %d g fruit in %d g honey (ratio %.2f:1)" % (FRUIT_G, HONEY_G, HONEY_G / FRUIT_G))
print("Creamed honey seed: %d g seed per %d g liquid honey" % (int(HONEY_G * SEED_PCT / 100), HONEY_G))
print("Keep infused honey dry: water invites fermentation.")
demo.expected_output:
Honey-preserved fruit: 500 g fruit in 500 g honey (ratio 1.00:1)
Creamed honey seed: 50 g seed per 500 g liquid honey
Keep infused honey dry: water invites fermentation.

title: Signature Comb-and-Cream Tasting Board
description: The Signature Comb-and-Cream Tasting Board is an original Signature serving design that presents comb honey as the centerpiece of a small tasting board, with clotted-style cream, warm bread, and apple slices arranged around it. The board is built for sharing: guests cut their own comb, spread cream on bread, and top it with comb honey, so the wax texture, the honey flavor, and the cream richness are tasted in one bite. The design keeps the comb whole until serving, so its capped cells are visible and the honey inside is seen before it is eaten, which is part of the pleasure. It is a simple, no-cooking design, and its Signature character is the comb-cream-bread-apple combination, chosen to show comb honey at its best rather than hiding it in a recipe.
ingredients: One piece of fully capped comb honey
method: Place the whole comb piece in the center of a board, with cream, bread, and apple slices around it.
Cut the comb at the table with a sharp knife, so guests see the capped cells before eating.
Spread cream on warm bread, top with a piece of comb, and eat at once.
Offer apple slices with comb honey for a lighter, fruit pairing.
Cover any leftover comb and store it at room temperature for the next day.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Comb honey is raw honey from a trusted beekeeper; it is never for infants under 12 months.
storage: Store leftover comb covered at room temperature; eat within a few days once cut, since exposed comb dries and picks up odors.
variations: Cheese board version: swap the cream for strong cheese and keep the bread and apples.
Solo version: comb honey on warm bread alone, for one person.
Party version: two comb pieces, one light and one dark, for comparison.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Comb-and-Cream Tasting Board'
FRAME_G = 900; PORTION_G = 45
portions = FRAME_G // PORTION_G
print("One frame of %d g comb honey gives %d portions of %d g" % (FRAME_G, portions, PORTION_G))
print("Leftover: %d g" % (FRAME_G - portions * PORTION_G))
print("Chew comb, swallow the honey, and spit out or swallow the wax as you prefer; wax is not digested.")

One frame of 900 g comb honey gives 20 portions of 45 g
Leftover: 0 g
Chew comb, swallow the honey, and spit out or swallow the wax as you prefer; wax is not digested.

title: Signature Orchard Switchel Cooler
description: The Signature Orchard Switchel Cooler is an original Signature take on the old haymaker's drink, rebuilt around apple juice and honey instead of plain water and sugar. It mixes apple juice, cider vinegar, grated ginger, and light honey into a tart, golden cooler that is made in a jug, chilled, and served over ice with apple slices. The design keeps the switchel balance of sweet, sour, and ginger heat, but the apple juice gives it a fruit body that water alone cannot, and the honey keeps it in the suite's theme. It is a summer drink, made ahead in a batch and kept refrigerated for the week.
ingredients: Apple slices and ice to serve
method: Warm the water gently and dissolve the honey in it, then cool to room temperature.
Stir in the apple juice, cider vinegar, and grated ginger.
Refrigerate for at least two hours so the ginger flavor develops.
Strain out the ginger, pour over ice, and garnish with apple slices.
Taste and adjust: add more honey for sweetness or more vinegar for tartness, a teaspoon at a time.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. This drink contains vinegar and is not suitable for infants or for young children in large amounts.
storage: Store the cooler refrigerated for up to five days; stir before serving, since ginger settles.
variations: Sparkling version: replace half the water with sparkling water at serving time.
Berry version: add a handful of crushed raspberries to the jug.
Winter version: serve warm, without ice, with a cinnamon stick.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Orchard Switchel Cooler'
RATIOS = [('Light', 1, 2), ('Classic', 1, 1), ('Rich', 2, 1)]
for name, honey, water in RATIOS:
    total = honey + water
    print("%s syrup: %d parts honey + %d parts water = %.0f%% honey" % (name, honey, water, honey / total * 100))
print("Rich 2:1 syrup keeps longer; 1:1 syrup mixes cold drinks fastest.")
demo.expected_output:
Light syrup: 1 parts honey + 2 parts water = 33% honey
Classic syrup: 1 parts honey + 1 parts water = 50% honey
Rich syrup: 2 parts honey + 1 parts water = 67% honey
Rich 2:1 syrup keeps longer; 1:1 syrup mixes cold drinks fastest.

title: Signature Golden Vinaigrette Trio
description: The Signature Golden Vinaigrette Trio is an original Signature set of three dressings built on one honey-vinegar base, so a cook learns one method and gains three dressings. The base is honey whisked into cider vinegar, then oil whisked in slowly, and the trio branches from there: mustard for a sharp green-salad dressing, orange juice for a bright fruit-salad dressing, and toasted sesame for a nutty grain-bowl dressing. Each dressing is made in a jar, shaken, and labeled, and the trio is designed to cover a week of salads from a single session. The Signature character is the shared base and the jar method, which makes the trio a system rather than three unrelated recipes.
method: Whisk the honey into the cider vinegar until dissolved.
Whisk in the oil slowly until the dressing thickens, then divide into three jars.
Stir mustard into the first jar, orange juice into the second, and sesame oil into the third.
Seal, label each jar, and refrigerate.
Shake well before serving, since chilled dressings separate.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Refrigerate promptly and discard any dressing left at room temperature for more than two hours.
storage: Store the trio refrigerated for up to a week; bring to room temperature for ten minutes before shaking and serving.
variations: Single dressing: make only the mustard version for everyday salads.
Herb version: add chopped dill or parsley to the mustard dressing.
Spicy version: add a pinch of chili flakes to the sesame dressing.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Golden Vinaigrette Trio'
OIL = 180; VINEGAR = 60; HONEY = 30
total = OIL + VINEGAR + HONEY
print("Dressing: %d ml oil, %d ml vinegar, %d ml honey = %d ml total" % (OIL, VINEGAR, HONEY, total))
print("Honey share: %.1f%%; oil share: %.1f%%" % (HONEY / total * 100, OIL / total * 100))
print("Whisk honey into the vinegar first; the emulsion holds longer.")
demo.expected_output:
Dressing: 180 ml oil, 60 ml vinegar, 30 ml honey = 270 ml total
Honey share: 11.1%; oil share: 66.7%
Whisk honey into the vinegar first; the emulsion holds longer.

title: Signature Calm-Skin Honey Ritual
description: The Signature Calm-Skin Honey Ritual is an original Signature skin-care routine for unbroken skin only, designed as a gentle weekly ritual rather than any kind of treatment. It pairs a honey-and-oat mask, a honey lip balm, and a honey bath soak, all built on mild honey and plain, well-known ingredients, with a patch test as the first step every time a new batch is made. The ritual is deliberately slow: mask for fifteen minutes, balm through the day, soak in the evening, so skin care becomes a routine rather than a quick fix. It makes no healing claims of any kind, it is never used on broken, infected, or irritated skin, and it stops at the first sign of redness or itching. Honey is not a cure for any disease. Nothing in this record diagnoses, treats, or replaces medical care; see a clinician for wounds that are deep, large, infected, slow to heal, or on the face, hands, feet, or genitals, and for any cough that is severe, bloody, or lasts more than a few weeks.
ingredients: Beeswax and plant oil for the balm
method: Patch test first: dab a little of the mask on the inner arm, wait twenty minutes, and proceed only if there is no redness or itching.
Mix one tablespoon of honey with one tablespoon of fine oatmeal and one tablespoon of plain yogurt for the mask.
Apply to clean, unbroken skin, rest for fifteen minutes, and rinse with warm water.
Apply the honey beeswax balm to lips as needed through the day.
For the soak, dissolve two tablespoons of honey in warm bath water and bathe as usual, then rinse.
safety: Honey is not a cure for any disease. Nothing in this record diagnoses, treats, or replaces medical care; see a clinician for wounds that are deep, large, infected, slow to heal, or on the face, hands, feet, or genitals, and for any cough that is severe, bloody, or lasts more than a few weeks. Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. For unbroken skin only; never apply to broken, infected, or irritated skin. Stop at once if redness, itching, or swelling appears.
storage: Store the mask ingredients separately and mix fresh each time; store the balm in a sealed tin at room temperature for up to three months.
evidence_grade: graded: honey for everyday skin softening mixed; honey as a treatment for any skin disease unproven
variations: Oat-only mask: honey and oatmeal with water instead of yogurt for sensitive skin.
Plain balm: beeswax balm without honey for days when skin is irritated.
Quick ritual: mask only, for weeks when there is no time for the full routine.

demo.code:

for use, grade in CLAIMS:
    print("%s: %s" % (use, grade))
print("Supported: %d, mixed: %d, unproven: %d" % (counts["supported"], counts["mixed"], counts["unproven"]))
print("Grades describe published evidence, not a promise of benefit.")

Honey bath for skin softening: mixed
Supported: 0, mixed: 3, unproven: 1
Grades describe published evidence, not a promise of benefit.

title: Signature Honey-Oat Bath Bars
description: The Signature Honey-Oat Bath Bar is an original Signature soap design that folds fine oatmeal through a honey soap base, so each bar exfoliates gently while the honey adds lather and a warm, golden color. The bars are made by the cold-process method with honey at five percent of the oil weight, oatmeal stirred in at trace, and a six-week cure, and they are cut thick so they last longer in the shower. The Signature character is the oatmeal-through-the-bar design rather than oatmeal only on top, which means the gentle texture lasts for the whole life of the bar instead of washing off in the first week. As with all lye soap, the bars are an adult project with gloves and eye protection, and they are for skin only.
ingredients: 700 g olive oil and 300 g coconut oil
Sodium hydroxide lye and water, weighed exactly
50 g honey (5 percent of oil weight)
Gloves, eye protection, molds, and a scale
method: Weigh all ingredients exactly and dissolve the lye in water with ventilation, gloves, and eye protection.
Cool the lye solution and the oils to room temperature, then mix until the soap thickens to trace.
Stir in the honey, then the oatmeal, and mix until evenly distributed.
Pour into molds, watch for overheating, and unmold after two days.
Cut into thick bars and cure for six weeks in a dry, ventilated place before use.
safety: Lye burns skin and eyes: gloves and eye protection are required, and children must stay away from lye. Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. For skin only, never for eating; stop using a bar if it irritates the skin.
storage: Store cured bars dry and ventilated; a dry bar lasts much longer than one left sitting in water.
variations: Plain version: leave out the oatmeal for a smooth honey bar.
Herb version: add dried rosemary at trace instead of oatmeal.
Gift version: wrap cured bars in parchment with a handwritten label.

demo.code:

title: Signature Seeded Honey Loaf and Breakfast Crunch
description: The Signature Seeded Honey Loaf and Breakfast Crunch is an original Signature pair built on one dough idea: a honey-seed loaf for slicing, and the same seeds and honey baked as a breakfast crunch for yogurt. The loaf is a soft wheat bread sweetened only with honey and studded with sunflower and pumpkin seeds, while the crunch toasts oats and the same seeds in honey and oil until crisp. The pair is designed as a week's breakfast from one baking session: loaf for toast, crunch for yogurt, both from the same pantry ingredients. The Signature character is the shared seed-and-honey pantry across bread and cereal, so nothing is bought for one half of the pair alone.
ingredients: 80 g mixed sunflower and pumpkin seeds
300 g rolled oats and 60 g oil for the crunch
method: Dissolve the honey in warm water, add yeast, and rest until foamy.
Mix in flour, salt, and seeds, knead until smooth, and rise until doubled.
Shape into a loaf, rise for forty minutes, and bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit until deep golden.
For the crunch, toss oats and seeds with honey and oil, bake at 300 degrees Fahrenheit, stirring every fifteen minutes, until crisp.
Cool both fully before slicing the loaf or storing the crunch.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Seeds and nuts are a choking hazard for young children; serve the crunch only to children old enough for seeds, or make a seed-free version.
storage: Store the loaf wrapped at room temperature for up to five days; store the crunch airtight for up to four weeks.
variations: Raisin loaf: add raisins to the dough with the seeds.
Berry crunch: stir dried berries into the cooled crunch.
Mini loaves: divide the dough into two small pans and bake for 30 minutes.

title: Signature Honey Clarity Lab
description: The Signature Honey Clarity Lab is an original Signature home-science project that turns honey crystallization into a small experiment anyone can run with two jars and a thermometer. One jar is kept warm and liquid, one is kept cool and allowed to crystallize, and the maker records how long each state lasts, how the texture changes, and how gentle warming restores the crystallized jar. The lab includes a simple water-activity estimate from the honey's water percentage, so the maker sees why honey resists spoilage in numbers, not just in words. It is a teaching design: the point is to observe crystallization as a normal, reversible sugar process, not as honey going bad, and to learn the safe warming limit by measuring it.
ingredients: Two jars of the same honey
method: Label one jar warm and one jar cool, and record the starting texture of both.
Keep the warm jar at room temperature and the cool jar in a cool room, and check both weekly, noting cloudiness and grittiness.
When the cool jar has crystallized, warm it gently in a water bath below 140 degrees Fahrenheit, stirring occasionally.
Record how long reliquification takes and how the texture compares with the warm jar.
Repeat the cycle once more to confirm that crystallization is reversible and repeatable.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Never heat a sealed jar that cannot vent, and never microwave honey in plastic. Discard any honey that bubbles or smells of alcohol.
storage: Store both lab jars sealed at room temperature between observations; the warm jar may crystallize too over time, which is itself an observation.
variations: Variety comparison: run the lab with two honey varieties side by side.
Temperature comparison: keep one jar cool and one jar cold to compare crystallization speed.
Creamed-honey lab: seed one jar deliberately and compare its texture with the naturally crystallized jar.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Signature Honey Clarity Lab'
WATER_PCT = [16, 17, 18, 20]; JAR_G = 350; CRYST_PCT = 90
for w in WATER_PCT:
    aw = 0.25 + 0.02 * w
    print("Water %.0f%% -> estimated water activity %.2f" % (w, aw))
mins = JAR_G * CRYST_PCT / 100 * 0.05
print("Reliquify %d g jar at %d%% crystallized: about %.0f minutes in warm (not boiling) water" % (JAR_G, CRYST_PCT, mins))
print("Estimates only; water activity below about 0.60 resists most microbial growth.")
demo.expected_output:
Water 16% -> estimated water activity 0.57
Water 17% -> estimated water activity 0.59
Water 18% -> estimated water activity 0.61
Water 20% -> estimated water activity 0.65
Reliquify 350 g jar at 90% crystallized: about 16 minutes in warm (not boiling) water
Estimates only; water activity below about 0.60 resists most microbial growth.

title: Signature Three-Honey Tasting Flight
description: The Signature Three-Honey Tasting Flight is an original Signature tasting design that arranges three honeys as a guided flight, from lightest to darkest, with a written score sheet and a food pairing for each honey. The flight opens with a light clover honey paired with plain yogurt, moves to a medium wildflower honey paired with apple slices, and closes with a dark honey paired with strong cheese, so each honey is tasted both neat and with food. The score sheet rates floral character, sweetness, and finish for each honey, and the flight ends with a ranked preference, which makes the tasting a decision: which honey suits tea, which suits baking, and which suits eating neat. The design is deliberately simple, needing only three honeys, three pairings, and one score sheet, so it works as a first tasting for anyone. Honey is not a cure for any disease. Nothing in this record diagnoses, treats, or replaces medical care; see a clinician for wounds that are deep, large, infected, slow to heal, or on the face, hands, feet, or genitals, and for any cough that is severe, bloody, or lasts more than a few weeks.
ingredients: Light clover honey, medium wildflower honey, and dark honey
Plain yogurt, apple slices, and strong cheese
Small spoons and a printed score sheet
method: Arrange the three honeys from lightest to darkest and label each dish.
Taste each honey neat first, and score floral character, sweetness, and finish from one to ten.
Taste each honey again with its pairing, and note whether the pairing lifts or covers the honey.
Cleanse the palate with water between honeys.
Rank the three honeys for tea, for baking, and for eating neat, and write the ranking on the score sheet.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. All three honeys are still honey: none is for infants under 12 months, and none is a medicine, however dark or expensive.
storage: Store the flight honeys sealed at room temperature after tasting; crystallization in any of them is normal and reversible.
evidence_grade: graded: dark honeys for wound care supported only as part of proper wound care, like other medical-grade honeys; any honey as a cure unproven
variations: Two-honey flight: clover and wildflower only, for a first tasting.
Fruit flight: pair all three honeys with different fruits instead of cheese.
Baking flight: bake three small cakes, one per honey, and taste the cakes side by side.

print("Highest average: %s" % best[0])

title: Signature Honey Pantry System
description: The Signature Honey Pantry System is an original Signature storage design built on three jars instead of one: a large sealed reserve jar that is never opened for daily use, a medium working jar for the table, and a small tasting jar for trying new varieties. The reserve jar stays sealed in a dark cupboard, so it crystallizes slowly and keeps its aroma, while the working jar is refilled from it with a clean, dry spoon, and the tasting jar holds only a few spoonfuls of each new honey for comparison. The system includes a yearly check, a reliquification routine for any jar that crystallizes, and a labeling rule that every jar carries its variety, source, and date. The Signature character is the three-jar discipline, which protects the reserve from moisture, heat, and daily handling, so the best honey stays at its best the longest.
ingredients: One large glass reserve jar with a tight lid
method: Fill the reserve jar, seal it, label it with variety, source, and date, and store it dark and cool.
Fill the working jar from the reserve jar with a clean, dry spoon, and use the working jar for daily honey.
Fill a tasting jar with a few spoonfuls of each new honey, label it, and taste before buying a large amount.
Check all jars yearly for bubbling, alcoholic smell, or sour taste, and discard any jar that shows those signs.
Reliquify any crystallized jar gently in warm water below 140 degrees Fahrenheit, stirring occasionally, until clear.
safety: Honey is not for infants under 12 months, because of the risk of infant botulism. This rule holds for every honey in this record, raw or heated, and for any food or drink made with honey that an infant might eat. Never heat a sealed jar that cannot vent, never microwave honey in plastic, and never feed honey to infants under 12 months.
storage: Store the reserve jar sealed in a dark, cool place for years; store the working jar at room temperature and refill it from the reserve, never with a wet spoon.
variations: Two-jar version: reserve and working jars only, for a small pantry.
Tasting set: six small jars for a honey-tasting shelf.
Gift version: a working jar and a tasting jar as a matched gift pair.
